key_insight: The ITE-Transformer combines EHR pre-training with causal machine learning to estimate how treatment effects may differ across individual patients.
clinical_relevance: The framework could support real-world comparative-effectiveness research by identifying patient characteristics associated with predicted treatment benefit.
method: Self-supervised transformer pre-training on longitudinal diagnosis and medication histories.
Prediction of treatment assignment and treatment-specific outcome risks from patient representations.
Doubly robust causal machine learning to estimate individualized treatment effects.
evidence_signal: Using structured EHRs from approximately 350,000 All of Us participants, evaluation in diabetes and pan-cancer cohorts showed better treatment-assignment and outcome-model discrimination and calibration than tabular models and a transformer without pre-training.
watch_item: Improved predictive performance does not establish accurate individual causal effects; observational estimates remain dependent on confounding and other causal assumptions.
paper_title: The ITE-Transformer: A pre-trained foundation model for predicting individualized treatment effects from electronic health records
